title: /deployments/health/read carries the last hour of the probe ring so a latency sparkline has a series to draw
description:
PREREQUISITE ROW spun out of task-df972c274f2a43eda3a9f57d2780c6f9 (the Environments surface) by worker-b1872f24 on 2026-09-07, which is BLOCKED on it. Parent id: task-df972c274f2a43eda3a9f57d2780c6f9.

THE GAP, MEASURED ON DISK, NOT INFERRED. The parent's DoD 1 requires "a latency sparkline over the last hour, driven by a REAL daemon frame". The served frame carries ONE point, not a series:
 - apps/daemon/src/http/deployments-health-read.ts:175-181 `lastProbeOf(probes)` returns `probes.at(-1)` only, and `DeploymentsHealthView.lastProbe` (:66-68) is `{at, latencyMs, status} | null`.
 - The FULL RING IS ALREADY AT THE PORT: `DeploymentsHealthSource.probes: readonly HealthProbe[]` (:86). The composition already supplies it. The view deliberately narrows it out.
So no new store read, no new route, no new composition edge is needed - this is a VIEW WIDENING plus its consumers.

WHY THE PARENT DID NOT JUST DO IT. Widening `DeploymentsHealthView` changes a RETURNED SHAPE, and its asserting consumers are outside that row's owned-path roster: apps/daemon/src/http/deployments-health-read.test.ts (20 arms, exact-shape toEqual) and apps/daemon/src/daemon-entry-deployments-health.test.ts (6 arms). The global roster rail says a worker who finds an unnamed consumer mid-step stops and reports rather than taking the extra path.

WHAT THIS ROW OWES. Project a BOUNDED, WINDOWED series - the last hour, not the whole 1440-row ring - so the browser is not handed 1440 points to draw 60. Name the window in the frame rather than leaving the client to infer it, or the client cannot assert it plotted the right span. The ring is bounded at 1440 rows per project/environment (task-cc05c473).

THE CONSUMER EDGE IS ALREADY BUILT AND WAITING. apps/control-room/src/live/live-deployments-health.ts decodes this frame EXACT-KEY at every level, so ADDING A KEY WILL RED IT - that is the property working as designed, and this row must update that decoder's key list and its test in the same edit, or the Environments section breaks. The renderer goes in apps/control-room/src/v2/ops/environments-section.tsx, which is already wired into the Health screen through live-environments.tsx and LiveHealth.

THE SPARKLINE ITSELF, per the parent's step 4 (unbuilt because it had no series): INLINE SVG, no charting dependency - `grep -rln 'sparkline|polyline' apps/control-room/src/v2 --include=*.tsx` finds no precedent, and a library for one sparkline is a bundle and a supply-chain edge for nothing. It must survive the degenerate inputs it meets on day one: ZERO points (a brand-new environment) renders an empty state and never an SVG with NaN coordinates; ONE point and all-identical latencies must not divide by a zero range. Give the SVG an accessible name and keep the numbers reachable as text or an attribute - a chart whose values exist only as path geometry cannot be asserted and cannot be read by a screen reader.

DERIVE NOTHING FROM THE SERIES. The parent's rail 1 stands: UP/DEGRADED/DOWN is the daemon's, and the series arriving in the browser is exactly the temptation to recompute it. environments-section.test.tsx already carries the disagreeing-frame arm that catches this; do not weaken it.

VERIFY: `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` AND `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon exec vitest run --root . --config package.json src/http/deployments-health-read.test.ts src/daemon-entry-deployments-health.test.ts`.
definitionOfDone: `DeploymentsHealthView` carries a BOUNDED latency series windowed to the last hour, projected from `DeploymentsHealthSource.probes` which the port already supplies. The window is stated IN the frame, not inferred by the client. Assert the projection drops rows older than the window by feeding a ring that spans more than an hour and asserting the returned count and the oldest returned instant - a projection that returns the whole ring passes any test that only checks the newest point.

Both asserting consumers are updated in the same edit and stay exact-shape: apps/daemon/src/http/deployments-health-read.test.ts and apps/daemon/src/daemon-entry-deployments-health.test.ts. Quote the count lines.

The control-room decoder apps/control-room/src/live/live-deployments-health.ts gains the new key in its exact-key list and its nested decoder, and its test asserts the series by value plus an EXTRA-key refusal on the nested series row. Adding the key WITHOUT this edit reds live-deployments-health.test.ts; state that you saw it red before fixing it, since that is the proof the exact-key discipline is real.

The sparkline is INLINE SVG in apps/control-room/src/v2/ops/environments-section.tsx with NO dependency added (assert package.json is untouched). Its degenerate inputs are asserted SEPARATELY: zero points renders the empty state and emits no NaN in any SVG attribute; one point renders without a division-by-zero; all-identical latencies render without a zero-range divide. Assert the plotted point COUNT matches the window so a sparkline drawing the whole ring is caught.
The SVG has an accessible name and its values are reachable as text or attributes, not only as path geometry.

The existing no-client-derivation arm in environments-section.test.tsx (the disagreeing-frame fixture) still passes UNWEAKENED, and a drill that recomputes the state from the new series reds it. Quote the drill outcome with a restore proof.
Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, the two named daemon files, and `pnpm typecheck`.
taskRails: RENDER WHAT THE DAEMON STATES, DERIVE NOTHING. Handing the browser the probe series is exactly the temptation to recompute UP/DEGRADED/DOWN from it. The daemon owns one opinion about one ring.

WINDOW THE SERIES SERVER-SIDE AND STATE THE WINDOW IN THE FRAME. The ring is 1440 rows; the sparkline wants the last hour. A client that slices an unwindowed ring cannot assert it drew the right span.

ADDING A KEY TO THIS FRAME REDS apps/control-room/src/live/live-deployments-health.ts BY DESIGN. Update the decoder and its test in the same edit; never widen the client to a subset match to avoid the red.
INLINE SVG, NO CHARTING DEPENDENCY. There is no chart precedent in this app and one sparkline does not justify a bundle or a supply-chain edge.
ASCII-ONLY SOURCES, APOSTROPHE-FREE JSX TEXT - an apostrophe in JSX reds the scheduler package-boundary scan in a distant lane.

implementationPlan.description: MEASURE BEFORE EDITING. No changes. Record verbatim: (a) `git status --porcelain -- apps/daemon/src/http apps/control-room/src` — note foreign dirt and continue; (b) `sed -n '62,78p' apps/daemon/src/http/deployments-health-read.ts` (the view) and `sed -n '178,182p'` (`lastProbeOf` returning `probes.at(-1)`), confirming the narrowing is where the row says and that `DeploymentsHealthSource.probes` at :86 already supplies the ring — if the view already carries a series, STOP: the gap is closed and the row must not build a duplicate; (c) `sed -n '166,186p' apps/control-room/src/live/live-deployments-health.ts` capturing the top-level exact-key list and the null-vs-unreadable discipline at :159-165; (d) `wc -l` on all six files, recording that `deployments-health-read.ts` is ALREADY at 251 against a 250 target, so step 2 must stay small; (e) read `apps/control-room/src/v2/shell/status-strip.tsx` around :12 — it CALLS something a sparkline without using SVG; see how it renders before inventing a look. Record the HEAD sha.

WIDEN THE FRAME, WINDOWED SERVER-SIDE, WITH THE WINDOW STATED IN IT. Add ONE new member to `DeploymentsHealthView` carrying the bounded series plus the window it was taken over — the window is a VALUE in the frame, not something the client infers, because that is what makes "it plotted the last hour" assertable at all (task rail 2). Project it from `source.probes`, which the port already supplies; add no store read, no route and no composition edge. Each point carries only what a sparkline needs (the instant and the latency) — do NOT copy `status` onto every point: the daemon owns exactly one opinion about the ring and repeating a per-point status invites the client to recompute the state from it (task rail 1). Keep the projection small and pure: `deployments-health-read.ts` is already 251 lines against a 250 target, so if the windowing needs more than a compact helper, put the helper beside it rather than growing this file toward 400. Newest-last ordering must match `lastProbeOf`'s `at(-1)` convention so the two members cannot disagree about which end is newest.

THE DAEMON ARMS, INCLUDING THE ONE THAT CATCHES AN UNWINDOWED RING. Update both exact-shape consumers in the same edit — `deployments-health-read.test.ts` (20 exact-shape arms) and `daemon-entry-deployments-health.test.ts` (6) — keeping them EXACT-shape rather than loosening any `toEqual` to a partial match. Then add the arm DoD 1 specifies: feed a ring SPANNING MORE THAN AN HOUR and assert BOTH the returned point COUNT and the OLDEST RETURNED INSTANT, because a projection that returns the whole ring passes any test that only checks the newest point. Add the boundary arms too: a probe exactly at the window edge, an EMPTY ring yielding an empty series with the window still stated, and a ring entirely older than the window yielding an empty series rather than a null member. Verify the windowing arm by mutating the projection to return the whole ring and confirming it goes RED, then restore.

SEE THE CLIENT RED, THEN FIX IT — DoD 3 asks for the observation, not just the fix. With step 2 landed and the decoder untouched, run `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` and RECORD `live-deployments-health.test.ts` FAILING, with the failing line quoted: that red is the exact-key discipline working, and seeing it is the only evidence the discipline is real rather than asserted. THEN update `live-deployments-health.ts`: add the key to the top-level `exactDataRecord` list at :169-171 and add a nested decoder for the series following the file's own shape — including the null-vs-unreadable rule at :159-165, where each nested decoder answers null for both and the raw member is re-checked at the top, so a MALFORMED series cannot read as an ABSENT one. Never widen the decoder to a subset match to avoid the red (task rail 3). In its test, assert the series BY VALUE and add an EXTRA-key refusal arm on the nested series row, so a row carrying an unexpected member is refused rather than silently accepted.

THE SPARKLINE, INLINE SVG, IN ITS OWN MODULE. New component module beside `environments-section.tsx` — not inline in it, because that file is 178 lines and an SVG with its degenerate branches lands it near 250, and a separate module gives the degenerate-input arms a seam to test directly. NO dependency is added; `package.json` must be untouched and asserted so. It renders the series the frame carries and NOTHING derived from it: no state, no colour keyed off a threshold the client invented (task rail 1). Handle the three degenerate inputs explicitly, because the first is day one: ZERO points renders the empty state and emits NO SVG at all rather than one with NaN coordinates; ONE point renders without dividing by a zero range; ALL-IDENTICAL latencies hit the same zero-range divide by a different route and must render too. Give the SVG an accessible name, and keep the values reachable as text or attributes — a chart whose numbers exist only as path geometry can be neither asserted nor read by a screen reader. ASCII-only source and NO apostrophe in any JSX text (task rail 5) — an apostrophe reds a scan in a distant lane this row's gates will not run.

WIRE IT IN AND PROVE NOTHING IS DERIVED — DoD 4's count assertion and DoD 6's drill. Render the sparkline from `environments-section.tsx` off the decoded frame. Assert the PLOTTED POINT COUNT matches the window the frame states, so a sparkline drawing the whole ring is caught — an SVG that rendered is not evidence it rendered the right span. Assert the three degenerate inputs SEPARATELY against the new module (zero / one / all-identical), checking the SVG ATTRIBUTE VALUES contain no `NaN`, since a NaN in a `points` or `d` attribute renders as nothing and passes a test that only asserts the element exists. Then DoD 6: confirm the existing disagreeing-frame arm in `environments-section.test.tsx` still passes UNWEAKENED, and DRILL it — make the component recompute the state from the new series and confirm that arm goes RED. Record the mutated path, the arm that reddened with its failure line, and the restore proof: `git diff -- <path>` empty for TRACKED files, SHA256 equality against an out-of-tree backup for the NEW module, taken in a call SEPARATE from the restore. A drill that does not redden means the guard is not load-bearing — fix the arm rather than recording a drill that proved nothing.

GATES AND ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW. Each leg FOREGROUND and STANDALONE; read the OUTPUT, not the exit code — no `Test Files N passed` line means nothing ran. Legs, quoted with count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`; the two named daemon files via `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon exec vitest run --root . --config package.json src/http/deployments-health-read.test.ts src/daemon-entry-deployments-health.test.ts`; and `pnpm typecheck`. Note that `pnpm test` covers NO `apps/**`, so it is not evidence for anything in this row. Repo-wide legs are a PATH-ATTRIBUTED BASELINE: merge-base failures, HEAD failures, delta intersected with owned paths must be EMPTY; disclose foreign red verbatim, never waive it. Then read the diff as an attacker: does the windowing arm still fail if the projection returns the whole ring (step 3 proved it — confirm the restore held)? Does any SVG attribute contain NaN for zero, one, or all-identical points? Is `package.json` byte-identical? Did any exact-shape `toEqual` get loosened to a partial match, or the client decoder to a subset? Is the state still read from the frame and never recomputed? comments.content:
PLANNING MEASUREMENT. The row's core claims all hold on disk; two notes for the worker and one small grep correction. HEAD, 2026-09-07.

1. CONFIRMED, BY READING. `deployments-health-read.ts:178-181` `lastProbeOf` returns `probes.at(-1)` only; `DeploymentsHealthView.lastProbe` (:66-68) is the single point; `DeploymentsHealthSource.probes` (:86) already carries the full ring. So this is a view widening plus consumers — no store read, no route, no composition edge. Both dependencies (task-cc05c473, task-509c6c16) are DONE.

2. THE DECODER RED IS REAL, and its lists are these: `live-deployments-health.ts:169-171` pins the top level to `["environment", "incident", "lastError", "lastProbe", "ok", "probeRefusal", "rollbackSha", "state"]`; the nested probe decoder at :128 pins `["at", "latencyMs", "status"]`. Worth carrying into the new nested decoder: the file's :159-165 discipline makes a NULL member and an UNREADABLE member deliberately different — each nested decoder answers null for both, and the raw member is re-checked at the top. Without that, a malformed series would read as an absent one.

3. GREP CORRECTION — the conclusion stands, the stated command does not. The description says `grep -rln 'sparkline|polyline' apps/control-room/src/v2 --include=*.tsx` finds no precedent. It actually returns TWO files (`status-strip.tsx` and its test), but the match is the WORD "sparkline" in a doc comment at status-strip.tsx:12, not an implementation. Measured separately: `grep -rn polyline apps/control-room/src/v2 --include=*.tsx` returns NOTHING, and `<svg` appears only in `context-bar.tsx` and `nav-rail.tsx` (icons). So there is genuinely no chart precedent and no library is warranted — the rail is right. This is the `mem:gotcha-a-widening-grep-needs-a-positive-control` corollary at file level: a grep result line cannot tell an implementation from a comment using the same word.

USEFUL LEAD from that same file, and the plan tells the worker to look: `status-strip.tsx` renders something it CALLS a sparkline with NO SVG at all. Read how before inventing a look — there may be an idiom worth matching for visual consistency.

4. TWO LINE BUDGETS ARE TIGHT, which shapes the plan. `deployments-health-read.ts` is ALREADY 251 lines against the 250 target (hard split at 400), so the windowing projection must stay compact or move to a helper beside it. `environments-section.tsx` is 178, and an inline SVG with its degenerate branches would land it near 250 — so the sparkline goes in its own module. That is not only cap arithmetic: a separate module gives the three degenerate-input arms a seam to test directly instead of through the whole section.

5. ONE DESIGN CALL WORTH STATING. Each series point carries only the instant and the latency — deliberately NOT a per-point `status`. The daemon owns exactly one opinion about the ring (task rail 1), and repeating a status on every point is precisely the material a client would recompute UP/DEGRADED/DOWN from. DoD 6's drill exists to catch that; do not hand it the ammunition.

6. THE TWO TESTS THAT PASS WHILE THE FEATURE IS BROKEN, both already named in the DoD and both carried into the plan as explicit arms: a projection returning the WHOLE ring passes any test that only checks the newest point (so the arm feeds a ring spanning more than an hour and asserts the count AND the oldest returned instant), and an SVG with `NaN` in a `points` or `d` attribute renders as nothing while passing a test that only asserts the element exists (so the degenerate arms assert the ATTRIBUTE VALUES, and all three cases are asserted separately).
